title: Retail energy price deregulation (SA 2013, NSW 2014, SEQ 2016): re-evaluation with electricity prices
design: Electricity prices relative to the CPI in each deregulating capital against capitals whose prices stayed regulated (Hobart, Canberra, Perth, Darwin), with class x quarter and city x quarter effects. Retailer counts are too few to use.
comparison: SA from 2013-Q1 against TAS/ACT/WA/NT; NSW from 2014-Q3 against TAS/ACT/WA/NT; QLD from 2016-Q3 against TAS/ACT/WA/NT
grade_reason: a pre-reform year of the primary outcome lies outside its 95% placebo band
headline: Not identified: electricity: prices relative to the CPI +9.4% (log points) (p = 0.024), saturated fixed effects.

category_summaries.prices: Electricity: prices relative to the CPI: +9.4% (log points) (p = 0.024; detectable from 9.1).

key_insights: The question: did removing retail electricity price caps (SA 2013, NSW 2014, south-east Queensland 2016) lower electricity prices?

The comparison: Electricity prices relative to the CPI in each deregulating capital against capitals whose prices stayed regulated (Hobart, Canberra, Perth, Darwin), with class x quarter and city x quarter effects. Retailer counts are too few to use.

What we found: the effect cannot be identified: a pre-reform year of the primary outcome lies outside its 95% placebo band, so the treated group was already moving apart before the reform. The registered layer's estimate (+9.4% relative to other prices) is not an effect.
How precise: only changes larger than about 9.1% relative to other prices could have been detected.

Compared with the earlier evaluation (2026-10-15, now archived): it found that the effect could not be identified (electricity: prices relative to the CPI +17.0% (log points)). The conclusion is unchanged; the smallest detectable effect is now 9.1, down from 9.5. This evaluation uses the estimator chosen in the blinded power study and the latest data.
What it means: these data cannot separate the reform from what was already happening.

method.summary: Saturated fixed effects on CPI classes by capital city and quarter, the layer chosen for this reform in the blinded power study, with every other layer reported side by side.

equations.label: Saturated fixed effects
equations.text: y_{cjq} = α_{cj} + δ_{cq} + γ_{jq} + β·D_{cjq} + ε_{cjq}

equations.label: Year by year
equations.text: y_{cjq} = α_{cj} + δ_{cq} + γ_{jq} + Σ_{k≠−1} β_{k}·1[q − T_{j} = k]·T_{cj} + ε_{cjq}

terms.meaning: 100 × log of the CPI class relative to All groups in city j, quarter q
1 for the reform's class in a treated state (or city) from its first exposed period to the end of its window
a level for each class in each state
each class's national movement in each period (industry cycles, product-wide price swings)
each state's movement in each period (state booms and slumps)

method.estimand: The average change in the outcome for the reform's classes in treated states over the window, beyond the same classes elsewhere and the treated states' other classes, net of the mean placebo estimate.
method.identification: Without the reform, the treated classes in treated states would have moved like the same classes elsewhere plus their states' other classes (parallel trends in the saturated model; for synthetic DiD, like the weighted comparison cells).
method.inference: The same estimator applied to up to 40 placebo industry groups (or CPI classes) at the reform's states and dates gives the no-effect distribution: the p-value is the share of centred placebo estimates at least as large; the 90% interval subtracts their 5th and 95th percentiles. Benjamini-Hochberg q-values across the specification's primary outcomes. Placebo states and fake dates check the reform's own classes.
steps: Registered the layer, outcomes, windows and placebo pools in the specification before any treated post-reform outcome was computed.
Design stage: hid treated cells from first exposure, computed every layer's placebo distribution, the own-class placebos and the pre-reform event-study check.
Committed the design and plan, ran a blinded dry run, then one registered run with treated cells restored.
Judged the registered layer's estimate against its placebo distribution; reported every other layer side by side.

panels.title: Panel A. Electricity: prices relative to the CPI, 100 × log points (primary outcome; 3 treated cells)

notes: Panel A: 100 × log of the CPI class relative to All groups, CPI class × capital city × quarter, unweighted; 2005-Q1 to 2019-Q2 (58 periods), 85 classes, 7 cities.

Each column applies one estimator to the same panel. β is the average effect on the reform's classes in treated states (cities) over the window, net of the mean of the same estimator across the placebo groups. Columns (6) and (7) compare the treated group's average with reweighted untreated cells over each cohort's window; their observations and units are summed over cohorts.

The placebo standard deviation is the spread of the same estimator across up to 40 placebo industry groups (or CPI classes) given the reform's states and dates: the randomization-inference analogue of a standard error. p-values rank the estimate among the centred placebo estimates; with 40 placebos the smallest attainable is about 0.024, so *** cannot occur. Clustered standard errors are not reported: with seven or eight states they are unreliable, and the registered inference uses placebos.

MDE: the smallest effect detectable with 80% power at the 5% level (2.8 × the placebo standard deviation). Placebo groups: placebo industry groups (business outcomes) or CPI classes (prices). Pre-trend test: every event-study coefficient with k ≤ −2 (saturated model, net of the placebo mean) lies inside its 95% placebo band; a failure means the outcome is not identified. BH q-value: Benjamini–Hochberg across the specification's primary outcomes.
